author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Police arrested two men and a 16-year-old boy as an anti-immigration march and counter-demonstration unfolded in Portsmouth, England, on Saturday. The city saw a large police deployment for a second consecutive weekend after disorder accompanied the arrival of a boat carrying 140 asylum seekers the previous Sunday.

A 76-year-old Southampton man was detained on suspicion of concealing his identity after officers invoked new powers requiring face coverings to be removed. A 33-year-old Portsmouth man was arrested on suspicion of obstructing a highway. The teenager was arrested on suspicion of violent disorder connected to the prior weekend, police said.

Opposing groups were assigned separate gathering areas before marching through the city center. Authorities said Saturday was largely peaceful outside a small number of incidents, in contrast with the earlier protest in which officers were assaulted and police vehicles and other property were damaged. A man charged over last weekend’s disorder also appeared in court Saturday. Police have said further arrests tied to those earlier scenes are expected, keeping the public-order investigation active.
dek: A large police operation separated an anti-immigration march and counter-demonstrators during a second weekend of tension.
headline: Three arrested as rival protests return to Portsmouth
